title: chaos-neutral failover coordinator: readiness quorum probes and adaptive model-downgrade matrix
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We frequently see partial-region degradations where traffic routing flips too aggressively or model variant fallbacks are too blunt (full downgrade instead of gradual degradation). This causes sudden QoS regressions for customers and expensive cold-start spikes in the warm-standby region.

Goal: Implement a 'chaos-neutral' failover coordinator that performs probabilistic quorum-based readiness probes and performs staged model-variant downgrades using an adaptive matrix. The coordinator should: (1) assess region readiness via multi-dimensional probes (capacity, warmed KV cache percentage, model variant priming score), (2) produce a readiness score with configurable thresholds per customer tier, (3) orchestrate staged traffic cutovers with progressive weight shifts, and (4) execute model-variant downgrades according to an adaptive matrix that prioritizes low-latency, quantized variants first, preserving semantic fidelity as much as possible.

Why different from prior work: Existing tickets addressed warm-standby priming and quorums in static ways. This ticket focuses on a probabilistic handshake, staged cutover with configurable dwell times, and a downgrade matrix that adapts based on rolling quality metrics (latency, token-accuracy regressions, and prefix-cache hit rate). It is explicitly designed to be tolerant to chaos exercises (simulated network partitioning) and to minimize customer-visible discontinuities.

Scope: PoC coordinator service + runtime hooks + console rollout controls + canary automation. Initial rollout limited to EU and us-west regions for customer tier PRO and above.

Out of scope: billing-tier automation, private on-prem deployments (will follow after hosted validation).
acceptance_criteria: Coordinator can compute a composite readiness score (0-100) for a candidate standby region using capacity, KV cache warmness, model-variant priming fraction, and health probe latencies
Configurable threshold per customer tier that gates staged traffic shifts (e.g., tier=PRO require readiness>=75)
Progressive traffic cutover supports fractional ramp steps (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) with configurable dwell and automated rollback on quality degradation
Model-downgrade matrix supports at least three fallbacks (full-fp32 -> int8-quant -> distilled-model) and applies the lowest-impact path based on recent eval delta metrics
Can simulate a controlled failover in a staging environment using the chaos harness with no more than 5% end-to-end request latency regressions compared to baseline
Dashboard displays readiness score components, active variant mapping, and post-cutover quality delta (latency and quality) within 30s of events
Automated runbook links and a one-click rollback in Console are present for operators
implementation_notes: Design: coordinator as a small stateful service (k8s deployment) with leader election per region-pair; leader maintains a rolling heatmap of probe outcomes

Readiness probes: (a) capacity query from scheduling plane, (b) KV cache coverage estimate derived from prefix-sampling, (c) model-variant warmness via lightweight token-generation primers (configurable prompt set), (d) health probe latency & error-rate
Scoring: use weighted aggregation with per-customer-tier weight profiles. Default weights: capacity=0.35, cache=0.30, priming=0.25, latency=0.10. Expose weight overrides via Console

Staged cutover: implement an ordered state machine: NO_SWITCH -> PREPARE -> TRAFFIC_RAMP -> OBSERVE -> FINALIZE -> ROLLBACK. Each transition driven by readiness thresholds and observed quality metrics

Downgrade matrix: maintain ranked list of candidate model variants per family. On cutover, try first compatible variant that satisfies latency SLO; if quality regression exceeds threshold, step to next variant and re-evaluate
Telemetry: emit events to Kafka (readiness.score, cutover.step, variant.switch, metric.delta) and ensure Console consumes them for live charts
Safety: implement a quorum check across 3 independent probe endpoints (control-plane, infra-agent, and synthetic traffic gateway) before critical transitions
Feature flag: rollout behind feature flag 'chaos_neutral_failover_v1' with per-org allowlist
Fallback behavior: if no standby meets readiness, coordinate gradual fallback to reduced-capacity mode within origin region with clear operator alerting
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives in readiness probes could cause unnecessary cutovers. Mitigation: require quorum across independent probe types and add hysteresis/dwell time before decisions

Risk: Model downgrades may cause semantic regressions. Mitigation: run lightweight semantic evals on priming prompts and compare to baseline; limit downgrade steps and provide immediate rollback trigger
Risk: Increased control-plane load during mass failovers. Mitigation: stagger probe schedules and throttle per-customer probing frequency; aggregate at the coordinator
Risk: Operator confusion during staged ramps. Mitigation: Console visualizations with clear step labels + one-click abort + alerting
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): deploy coordinator in staging and run chaos experiments for EU/us-west pairs (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (Pilot): enable for 5 internal customers in PRO tier in EU region with feature flag, monitor for 30 days.
Phase 2 (Gradual rollout): open to all PRO customers in us-west + EU after fixes from pilot (2-4 weeks), expose Console controls.
Phase 3 (GA): enable for standard tiers with conservative thresholds and provide opt-out. Ship runtime-1.20 with docs and runbook.
comments: 2026-03-10 | Ava Chen: Created ticket. Added initial design notes and acceptance criteria. Assigned to Rafael for implementation. Added dependencies on existing quorum and priming work.

2026-03-11 | Rafael Ortiz: Spike complete. Proof-of-concept leader election + probe collector is running in dev. Observed that prefix-sampling for KV warmness adds ~15% additional probe cost; exploring sampling reduction heuristics.
2026-03-11 | Priya Nair (Reviewer): Feedback: make weight profiles per-customer-shard, not global. Also add SLO guardrails for downgrade latency targets. See Confluence comment thread.

2026-03-12 | Rafael Ortiz: Updated scoring to support per-tenant overrides and added ability to pin weight profiles to releases. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/482 (WIP)
2026-03-12 | SRE Team Lead (Liam Brooks): Concern: telemetry volume. Rafael to add aggregation and a 1m sampling window to reduce event churn. Marked for SRE review.
